results.title: What Goes into a Charter for DSMB or Endpoint Adjudication? - Advarra
results.content: After 20 years of supporting clinical trial sponsors, the team at Advarra knows success depends on having a good committee charter. Independent data monitoring committees (DMCs/DSMBs) and endpoint adjudication committees (EACs/CECs) rely on the charter to set the course for project and the conduct of the committees. Where the clinical protocol outlines clinical trial operations and conduct details, the charter does the same to guide the operations and actions of the associated DMC and/or EAC supporting the trial. In this blog, and in practice, we talk about a “charter” because that is the term the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) uses in its 2006 guidance on data monitoring committees, which governs how DMC and EACs operate. However, the charter document is also seen as an operating plan, operations manual, or similar instructions document describing how the DMC or EAC will independently oversee and assess the research as it is carried out. Also, keep in mind, both FDA and European Medicines Agency (EMA) consider the charter to have the same level of importance as the clinical trial protocol itself. … FDA may request that the sponsor submit the charter to FDA well in advance of the performance of any interim analyses, ideally before the initiation of the trial” FDA guidance “Establishment and Operation of Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees,” section 4.3. DMC and EAC must be set up and operational prior to the protocol initiating, and a key part of the setup process is formulating the charter. The charter is the detailed operating plan for how your DMC or EAC will review and oversee the trial. Developing the charter is also a good time for the DMC and EAC expert medical and clinical research professionals to offer the sponsor suggestions for potentially incorporating more efficient or meaningful endpoints and measurements into the protocol. Anyone involved with clinical research for any period of time knows the process of conducting a clinical trial requires a lot of planning, protocols, operating procedures, and charters to map out what will happen, who will do what and when, and the expected outcomes and results.

results.title: [PDF] NIA Adverse Event and Serious Adverse Event Guidelines
results.content: Serious Adverse Event (SAE): Any adverse event that: • Results in death • Is life threatening, or places the participant at immediate risk of death from the event as it occurred • Requires or prolongs hospitalization • Causes persistent or significant disability or incapacity • Results in congenital anomalies or birth defects • Is another condition which investigators judge to represent significant hazards Unanticipated Problem (UP): Defined by DHHS 45 CFR part 46 as any incident, experience, or outcome that meets all of the following criteria: • unexpected, in terms of nature, severity, or frequency, given (a) the research procedures that are described in the protocol-related documents, such as the IRB-approved research protocol and informed consent document; and (b) the characteristics of the study population; • related or possibly related to participation in the research (in this guidance document, possibly related means there is a reasonable possibility that the incident, experience, or outcome may have been caused by the procedures involved in the research); • suggests that the research places participants or others at a greater risk of harm (including physical, psychological, economic, or social harm) than was previously known or recognized.

results.content: **Dsmb Report Template.** The DSMB ought to independently make recommendations for improving the performance of the scientific trial or terminating the trial if it determines the examine can be unable to offer helpful knowledge, regardless of modifications. The NIAMS and DSMB/OSMB SO will review the data concurrently provided by the investigator, typically contained in an SAE type, and independently assess the relationship of events to study/intervention. For extra data, see the NIAMS Reportable Events Requirements and Guidelines for Investigators Conducting NIAMS-Funded Clinical Research Studies. The DSMB/OSMB SO is the designated DSMB/OSMB member responsible for reviewing all SAEs and different expedited reports (e.g., UPs, protocol deviations impacting the protection of the research participants) as quickly as they are reported by the investigator.

results.title: AE vs. SAE: Reporting & Compliance Essentials
results.content: ## Why Proper Classification of Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) is Critical in Clinical Trials. Adverse events (AEs) are an inevitable part of clinical trials, but misclassifying or failing to report them properly can have serious consequences. Regulatory authorities, ethics committees, and sponsors expect accurate AE and SAE reporting to ensure patient safety, regulatory compliance, and the integrity of trial data. For Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) and Clinical Research Coordinators (CRCs) transitioning to sponsor-side roles, distinguishing between AEs and SAEs and ensuring proper reporting is one of the most essential responsibilities. ✅ Understand regulatory timelines for AE/SAE reporting. A Serious Adverse Event (SAE) is an AE that meets at least one of the following regulatory criteria:. 🚨 Regulatory Requirement: SAEs must be reported immediately to the sponsor, ethics committee, and regulatory authorities per GCP guidelines. 🚨 Regulatory Tip: If you are uncertain whether an AE qualifies as an SAE, escalate it to the medical monitor for review. ## Step-by-Step Guide to AE and SAE Reporting. ✔ If YES → It is an SAE and must be reported immediately. ✔ If NO → Document as an AE and continue monitoring. ✔ Use Sponsor SAE Reporting Forms. 🚨 Common Compliance Risk: Late or missing SAE reports can lead to serious regulatory consequences. ## Common AE and SAE Reporting Mistakes (and How to Avoid Them). 🚨 CRA Best Practice: Conduct regular site training sessions on AE/SAE classification and reporting requirements. ## Best Practices for CRAs to Ensure AE/SAE Compliance. ✔ Use an AE/SAE Decision Tree – Provide sites with flowcharts for event classification. ✔ Implement Real-Time SAE Tracking – Require sites to log all AEs in real time. ✔ Train Sites on Reporting Requirements – Conduct refresher training on SAE submission deadlines. ✔ Review Source Documents During Monitoring Visits – Ensure all AEs are recorded accurately in medical records. 🚨 Regulatory Compliance Tip: Always document SAE compliance efforts in monitoring reports and Trial Master File (TMF) records. ## Final Thoughts on Mastering AE/SAE Reporting as a CRA. Proper AE and SAE reporting is critical to patient safety, regulatory compliance, and trial success. ✔ Improve site compliance with safety reporting guidelines. ## More articles by Alvin Cheeks.

results.content: ### CRF 2 Left Nav : CTC. + Extended Database Management and Analysis. ## Event Adjudication and DSMB. ## Event Adjudication Committees and DSMBs Comprise Seasoned Experts. The value of any clinical research program hinges on the relevance of the research findings and the validity of the data. CRF has a strong reputation in the cardiovascular industry, has privileged access to many well-qualified and leading physicians, and serves as the alliance between sponsors and the committees. At a time when regulatory authorities place greater emphasis on the use of oversight committees, the CRF Clinical Trials Center provides first-rate event adjudication and DSMB services. ### Event Adjudication and DSMB. * Our Clinical Event Committees (CEC) systematically identify, adjudicate, and classify clinical endpoint events to ensure they are consistent with prevailing standards; the CRF Clinical Trials Center has CEC experience with more than 350 trials. * Our Data and Safety Monitoring Boards (DSMB) expertly monitor patient safety and treatment efficacy data to provide a risk-benefit profile of the investigative treatment or procedure throughout the life of the trial; the CRF Clinical Trials Center has DSMB experience with more than 100 trials. Member rosters include highly accredited, independent interventional cardiologists, noninterventional cardiologists, cardiothoracic surgeons, neurologists, and other specialists as well as biostatisticians. The CRF Clinical Trials Center Event Adjudication and Reporting Division is led by experts in the field who are committed to ensuring that trial data is consistent, reliable, and of high quality. **Our comprehensive CEC and DSMB services include:**. * Identification, recruitment, and contracting with committee members. * Development of committee charter, forms, and case dossiers. * Meeting scheduling, conduct, and reporting. * Entry of adjudication results into CRF or sponsor database. * Independent statistical output for DMC meetings. + Extended Database Management and Analysis.
